title: Clothes, and Hot and Cold
overview:
Name what you are wearing.
Say what the weather is doing.
Say: I am wearing a coat.
Put on a coat when it is cold.
functions: Say what you are wearing now
Ask what the weather is like
Say put on and take off
Say a thing is too big or too little
learningPath: Patterns: I am wearing, and it is raining.
Write about a hot day and a cold day.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 9. Look at your clothes.
Today you name what you are wearing.
A shirt. Trousers. Shoes. A coat.
Say them with me. Shirt. Trousers. Shoes. Coat.
A hat. A dress.
And the word for all of them: clothes.
Clothes is always more than one.
You never say one clothe.
Now the verb. Wear.
I wear a coat in winter.
And for right now: I am wearing a coat.
Say it with me. I am wearing.
Now the weather. This is why you choose clothes.
It is hot. It is cold.
Say them with me. Hot. Cold.
It is raining. It is windy.
The sun is out. It is a dry day.
And the question. What is the weather like?
It is cold and wet.
Last, two useful pairs.
Put on. Take off.
It is cold, so put on your coat.
It is hot, so take off your coat.
And: this coat is too big.
Too big means bigger than you need.
That is Unit 9. Go and look out of the window.

grammar.title: I am wearing
grammar.explanation:
Two ways to talk about clothes.
One for every day. One for right now.
grammar.rule:
Every day:  I wear a coat in winter.
Right now:  I am wearing a coat.

I am wearing
You are wearing
He is wearing
She is wearing
grammar.workedExample:
Somebody asks what you have on.
1. They mean right now.
2. So use am wearing, not wear.
3. Start: I am wearing.
4. Then the thing: a blue shirt.
5. Say: I am wearing a blue shirt.
grammar.mistake:
No: I wearing a shirt.
English needs am, is or are before wearing.
Yes: I am wearing a shirt.
grammar.tip: Right now: am wearing. Every day: wear.
grammar.practice:
Write wear or am wearing.
1. Right now I ___ a shirt.
2. In winter I ___ a coat.
3. Today I ___ black shoes.
4. Every day I ___ the same trousers.
grammar.answers:
1. am wearing
2. wear
3. am wearing
4. wear
All four? You can talk about now and about every day.

grammar.title: It is hot. It is raining.
grammar.explanation:
The weather always starts with it.
There is no other word for it.
grammar.rule:
It is hot.
It is cold.
It is wet.
It is dry.

It is raining.
The sun is out.
There is a strong wind.

Question: What is the weather like?
grammar.workedExample:
You look out of the window and see rain.
1. Start with it.
2. Then is.
3. Then the weather word: raining.
4. Say: It is raining.
5. Add more: It is raining and it is cold.
grammar.mistake:
Do not leave out it.
No: Is hot today.
Yes: It is hot today.
Every language does this differently. English needs it.
grammar.practice:
Make a weather sentence.
1. hot
2. cold
3. wet
4. raining
5. dry
grammar.answers:
1. It is hot.
2. It is cold.
3. It is wet.
4. It is raining.
5. It is dry.
All five? Check that every one starts with it.

grammar.title: Put on and take off
grammar.explanation:
Two verbs of two words.
The second word carries the meaning.
grammar.rule:
Put ON your coat.    (start wearing)
Take OFF your coat.  (stop wearing)

Put on your shoes.
Take off your shoes.

You can also split them:
Put your coat on.
Take your coat off.
grammar.workedExample:
You come inside and it is warm.
1. You want to stop wearing your coat.
2. That is take off.
3. Say: I take off my coat.
4. Or split it: I take my coat off.
5. Both are correct.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say: I put my coat.
The word on is not optional.
Yes: I put on my coat.
grammar.tip: On means start. Off means stop.
grammar.practice:
Put on or take off?
1. It is cold outside. ___ your coat.
2. You come inside. ___ your coat.
3. It is raining. ___ a hat.
4. Your shoes are wet. ___ your shoes.
5. It is hot now. ___ your jumper.
6. You go out in the sun. ___ a hat.
grammar.answers:
1. Put on
2. Take off
3. Put on
4. Take off
5. Take off
6. Put on
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.title: Too big, too little
grammar.explanation:
Too is not the same as very.
Very is good. Too is a problem.
grammar.rule:
The coat is very big.   (it is a big coat)
The coat is too big.    (it does not fit me)

too big / too little
too long / too short
too hot / too cold
grammar.workedExample:
You try a coat and it does not fit.
1. It is bigger than you need.
2. That is a problem, so use too.
3. Say: It is too big.
4. Then ask for help: Have you a smaller one?
5. Do not say very big. That is not a problem.
grammar.mistake:
Very big is a description.
Too big is a complaint.
In a shop, the difference matters.
grammar.tip: Too means it is a problem.
grammar.practice:
Very or too?
1. This coat does not fit. It is ___ big.
2. That is a ___ nice dress.
3. I cannot drink this. It is ___ hot.
4. The sun is ___ hot today. I like it.
grammar.answers:
1. too
2. very
3. too
4. very
All four? You can complain in a shop now.

readings.title: A Cold Morning
readings.genre: A short text about getting ready
readings.setting: A flat, early on a winter morning
readings.passage:
It is cold this morning.
I look out of the window.
It is raining.
I put on a warm shirt.
I put on my black trousers.
I put on my coat and my hat.
I take my bag.
My shoes are by the door.
Now I am ready.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Name your clothes
speaking.instructions:
Look at what you are wearing.
Name each thing out loud.
Say the colour too if you can.
Like this: a blue shirt, black trousers, brown shoes.
Tap the mic. Name five things.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: colour before the thing?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor three things you are wearing. Ask what it would wear today.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — I am wearing
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about right now.
1. I am wearing a ___.
2. I am wearing ___.
3. I am not wearing a ___.
4. Today I am wearing ___.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: am before wearing every time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what it thinks people are wearing today.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say four lines about right now.
One. I am wearing a ...
Two. I am wearing ...
Three. I am not wearing a ...
Four. Today I am wearing ...
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: am before wearing every time?

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — What is the weather like?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: What is the weather like? B: It is cold and wet.
2. A: Is it raining? B: Yes, it is raining.
3. A: Take a coat. B: Thank you. Good idea.
4. A: And a hat. B: Yes. It is very cold.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: does every weather line start with it?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what the weather is like. Say what it is like where you are.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Put on, take off
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say put on or take off.
1. It is cold outside.
2. You come inside and it is warm.
3. It is raining.
4. Your shoes are wet.
5. The sun is very hot.
6. You go to bed.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: put on, take off, put on.
Then: take off, put on, take off.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what to put on for a cold and wet day.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — It is too big
speaking.instructions:
You are in a shop. Read A. Say B.
1. A: Try this coat. B: Thank you. It is too big.
2. A: This one? B: It is too little now.
3. A: And this one? B: That is good. How much is it?
4. A: Twenty. B: I will take it. Thank you.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: too, not very?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for a bigger size. Use too little in your ask.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The clothes that are always plural
speaking.instructions:
Some clothes are always more than one.
Listen and repeat.
trousers ... shoes ... clothes
You never say one trouser.
You say a pair of trousers.
Now say these lines.
My trousers are black.
My shoes are wet.
My clothes are dry.
Tap the mic. Say all three.
Check: did you say are, not is?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for three clothes words that are always plural.

writing.title: Writing 1 — What I am wearing
writing.prompt:
Write four lines.
Say what you are wearing right now.
Put the colour before the thing.
writing.model:
I am wearing a blue shirt.
I am wearing black trousers.
I am wearing brown shoes.
I am not wearing a hat.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
Am wearing in each one.
A colour in at least two.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add one line about what you wear to work.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A hot day and a cold day
writing.prompt:
Write six lines.
Three about a hot day. Three about a cold day.
Say the weather and what you wear.
writing.model:
It is hot.
I wear a shirt and no coat.
I take a bottle of water.

It is cold.
I put on a coat and a hat.
I take an umbrella.
writing.criteria:
Six lines.
Three for hot and three for cold.
Every weather line starts with it.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.support: Write three lines only, about one kind of day.
writing.extension: Add a line about what you do when it rains.

4. You wear it over your clothes when it is cold. ___

6. A woman wears it. It is one piece. ___

activities.answers:
1. a hat
2. shoes
3. trousers
4. a coat

activities.title: Practice 2 — Wear or am wearing?
activities.instructions:
Write wear or am wearing.
1. Right now I ___ a shirt.
2. In winter I ___ a coat.
3. Today I ___ black shoes.
4. Every day I ___ the same bag.
5. Right now I ___ no hat.
6. On hot days I ___ a light shirt.
activities.answers:
1. am wearing
2. wear
3. am wearing
4. wear
5. am wearing
6. wear
Five or six right: good. Right now takes am wearing.

activities.title: Practice 3 — What is the weather?
activities.instructions:
Make a weather sentence.
1. hot
2. cold
3. wet
4. dry
5. raining
6. windy
activities.answers:
1. It is hot.
2. It is cold.
3. It is wet.
4. It is dry.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Put on or take off?
activities.instructions:
Choose the right one.
1. It is cold outside. ___ your coat.
2. You come inside. ___ your coat.
3. It is raining. ___ a hat.
4. Your shoes are wet. ___ your shoes.
5. It is hot now. ___ your jumper.
6. You go out in the sun. ___ a hat.
activities.answers:
1. Put on
2. Take off
3. Put on
4. Take off
5. Take off
6. Put on
Five or six right: good.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Very or too?
activities.instructions:
Write very or too.
1. This coat does not fit. It is ___ big.
2. That is a ___ nice dress.
3. I cannot drink this. It is ___ hot.
4. The sun is ___ warm today. I like it.
5. These shoes hurt. They are ___ little.
activities.answers:
1. too
2. very
3. too
4. very
5. too
Four or five right: good. Too always means a problem.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read the notice
activities.instructions:
Read What to Wear Here again.
1. What two things must you wear?
2. What two things must you not wear?
3. What do you do with your coat?
4. Where does your bag go?
5. Can you wear open shoes?
activities.answers:
1. A clean shirt and strong shoes
2. Open shoes and a long coat
3. Take it off inside
4. Under your desk
5. No
Four or five right: you can read a workplace notice.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: You wear them on your feet. They are ___.
quizzes.why: Shoes go on your feet. Trousers go on your legs.

quizzes.q: You wear it on your head. It is ___.
quizzes.why: A hat goes on your head.

quizzes.q: Right now I ___ a blue shirt.
quizzes.why: Right now takes am wearing. Every day takes wear.
A weather sentence starts with it and needs is.
What is the weather like? is the usual question.

quizzes.q: It is cold outside. ___ your coat.
quizzes.why: Put on means start wearing. The word on is not optional.

quizzes.q: You come inside and it is warm. ___ your coat.
The coat does not fit you. It is ___ big.
quizzes.why: Too means it is a problem. Very is just a description.
Very is a description. Too would mean it is a problem.

quizzes.q: Which word is always more than one?
quizzes.why: Trousers, shoes and clothes are always plural.
Clothes is always plural, so it takes are.

quizzes.q: Water that falls from the sky is ___.
quizzes.why: Rain falls. Wind is air that moves.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

They are taught as one unit because that is how an adult meets them: you look out of the window and then you choose what to put on. The reading A Cold Morning does exactly that sequence and is worth doing before the vocabulary drills.
Trousers, shoes and clothes have no singular, so a learner will say my trouser is black for a long time. The repair is are, not is, and it is easiest to fix here where all three appear together.

teacherNotes.type: Too is a complaint, very is a description
teacherNotes.note: This is the pattern a learner needs in a shop and it is not obvious from either word. A learner who says this coat is very big when they mean it does not fit will be handed the same coat again.

teacherNotes.type: It is raining has no subject in many languages
teacherNotes.note: A learner will drop the it and say is raining. It is not carelessness; their own language does not need a subject there. Say that out loud and the correction stops feeling arbitrary.

assignment.title: What I wear, and what the weather is
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say five things you are wearing now.
Then say what the weather is like today.
2. Write six lines: three about a hot day, three about a cold day.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
